Exposed Technic-beam endoskeleton — the mech's upper arm built on 11L Technic liftarms cross-braced with 3L axle-pins, armor-panels clipped over the outer face leaving the inner beam-frame fully readable at the elbow gap, deliberate engineering on display.

Ball-joint + ratchet articulation — hips and shoulders seated on friction ball-joints (part 92013) while ratchet-joints lock the knees mid-stride, holding a lunging attack-pose under the mech's full brick weight, the poseable hard-suit hallmark locked tight.

CCBS shell-armor over Technic frame — large Hero-Factory CCBS body-shells (part 90650) snapped over a Technic-bone spine to clad the torso in smooth organic curves, the constraction-method blending system bricks below with flowing armor above, seam legible at every joint.

SNOT layered chest armor — wedge-slope panels and 2×4 smooth-tiles mounted sideways on SNOT brackets at the breastplate, overlapping like faceted ablative armor-plates with crisp recessed panel-lines between each layer, the hard-edged mecha surface built in system bricks.

Trans-cyan power-core reactor — a chest reactor built from trans-cyan 2×2 round-bricks stacked inside a dark-grey Technic-frame cavity, light-piping bar-elements (part 41530) routed through armor-gaps down to the forearms, the glowing energy-conduit signature of a lit MOC.

Hydraulic-piston knee greebles — pneumatic-cylinder elements (part 4697) flanked by 2L Technic-pin connectors detail the mech's knee-actuators, reading as pressurized hydraulic rams bracing the joint under load, dense powered-machinery greeble packed into a compact brick assembly.

Panel-line vent detailing — shoulder-armor broken with rows of 1×1 cheese-slopes inset between grille-tiles and exposed Technic-pin vents, the surface density of a convention-grade build, every panel reading as heat-exhaust or sensor-array in legitimate LEGO elements.

Cockpit-reveal canopy — a large trans-clear 6×4 curved canopy hinged open at the mech's upper torso, exposing a pilot minifig seated at a greebled instrument panel of 1×1 round-tiles and clip-mounted radar-dishes, the human-scale anchor inside the titan confirmed.

Weapon-arm cannon integration — a forearm cannon built from stacked 2×2 round-bricks on a 6L axle-barrel tipped with a trans-blue cheese-slope muzzle, the whole assembly mounted on a ball-joint wrist allowing full aim-posing without brick-stress, clean weapon-form in system parts.

Reverse-joint bird-leg digitigrade build — scout-mech legs bent backward at a ratchet-knee using a reversed 5L liftarm, terminating in clawed splay-feet built from clip-hinge plates, the crouched fast-walker stance engineered in Technic-joints with aggressive forward weight-distribution.

Modular swappable shoulder-packs — artillery missile-pods clipped onto a core shoulder-frame via bar-and-clip connections, visibly swappable for jump-jet modules built from 2×4 curved-slopes, the AFOL modular-mech loadout design readable in the exposed clip-points flanking the pauldron.

Battle-damage exposed frame — a deliberate missing chest-panel revealing the inner 7L liftarm frame below, a dark trans-orange 1×1 round-tile standing in for a damaged power-cell, scorched dark-grey grille-tiles flanking the breach, the war-torn salvage aesthetic built intentionally in brick.

Layered pauldron SNOT construction — shoulder-guards built as three overlapping 2×3 wedge-slope layers mounted on SNOT brackets angled outward, the staggered offsets creating thick armored pauldron geometry with shadow-gaps between each plate, the mecha shoulder-mass achieved in stacked system slopes.

Ankle-tilt posing via ball-joint — mech feet seated on single ball-joints (part 57518) allowing ankle-tilt compensation when posing on uneven display surfaces, flat-tile heel-spurs stabilizing the stance, the full-mech center-of-gravity managed through legitimate friction-joint brick engineering.

Beam-blade melee weapon build — a trans-lime 8L lightsaber-bar socketed into a hilt built from 1×2 Technic-pin-hole bricks and silver clip-tiles, mounted on a clip-hinge wrist for angled strike-posing, the energy-blade weapon read entirely from standard trans and system elements.

Light-piping eye-visor — the mech's head built with a dark-visor recess behind which a trans-red 1×4 bar element runs end-to-end, catching ambient light and reading as an illuminated sensor-strip, zero electronics required, pure optical light-piping in a legitimate LEGO element.

Greebled hip-actuator assembly — the hip-joint flanked by two 3L Technic-axle connectors plus a pneumatic-T-piece (part 4694) standing in as a servo-motor housing, surrounded by 1×1 round-plates for rivet-detail, the powered hip-swivel machinery fully legible in dense brick greeble.

Stacked wedge-slope shin-armor — lower-leg armor built from ascending 2×4 wedge-slopes stacked in opposing directions on a Technic-beam shin-core, the faceted angular geometry reading as ballistic-rated armor panels, the mass and forward-lean of a heavy-mech greave in pure system bricks.

Spine-column vertebrae detailing — the mech's exposed back-spine built from alternating 1×2 Technic-brick and ball-socket elements running up the torso centerline, each vertebra slightly offset, the mechanized spine reading as articulated structural anatomy through a brick-built column.

Missile-pod shoulder integration — a six-cell missile-pod built from a 2×3 plate base with six 1×1 round-bricks topped by trans-orange 1×1 round-plates as warhead-tips, the whole pod clipped onto a bar-socket shoulder-hardpoint, the fire-mission load-out read in system parts.

Forearm shield SNOT-plating — a rectangular forearm-shield built on a 4×6 plate base with 2×2 smooth-tiles and 1×2 grille-tiles mounted SNOT sideways to face the display angle, the flat-faceted deflection-surface geometry clean and hard-edged, no studs visible on the strike-face.

Neck-turret ball-joint head-mount — the mech head seated on a single Technic ball-joint housing allowing 360-degree yaw plus tilt, the joint visible beneath a collar ring of 1×1 cheese-slopes, the poseable sensor-head orientation a deliberate and visible articulation choice.

Trans-blue thruster-nozzle jet-pack — a jet-pack built from 2×2 round-bricks with trans-blue 1×1 cone-bricks as nozzle-exits, mounted on clip-hinges at the upper back for tilt-posing, the burn-direction adjustable and the energy-color coordinated with the trans-cyan chest power-core.

Technic-pin exposed rivet surfacing — dark-grey 1×2 Technic-bricks with open-pin-holes left exposed across the mech's torso flanks as rivet-detail rows, the visible circular pin-holes reading as industrial fasteners and giving the surface that assembled-steel-hull density without leaving system-brick studs showing.

Clip-hinge articulated tail-stabilizer — a heavy-mech counterbalance tail built from three 1×3 clip-hinge plates linked in a chain, terminating in a 2×4 wedge-slope counterweight, each hinge-segment poseable independently, the dynamic tail-balance both functional for display-posing and visually mechanical.
